text: Existing code is staged as Git would commit it (#391, #395). Inside a Git work tree, StagePythonApplication and the shared copiers, copyTree and StagePackage, select files from git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard, copy their working-tree bytes, leave out deleted tracked files and refuse submodules and nested repositories, so a checkout stages what a fresh clone in CI does. The Python application stager refuses by name every declaration Git ignores, its root's included. Outside Git the stagers walk the directory as before, and so do the shared copiers in a root the repository ignores with nothing tracked under it, such as synthesize's output under out/. The copiers skip a symlink in either mode, where the Python application stager refuses one. Receipts and fingerprints record the selection, git or directory, and HashExisting hashes what StagePackage staged. This replaces D-0181's staging of the whole application; every consumer still shares the one snapshot (D-0180, D-0199).
